title: Simultaneous Equations: Two Unknowns, Two Equations

blocks.title: 1. The Core Concept: Two Mysteries at Once
blocks.content: One equation with one unknown gives you one answer. But what if you have TWO unknowns (x AND y)? You need TWO equations to find them both. **Simultaneous equations** are a pair of equations that are both true at the same time. Solving them gives you the ONE pair of values (x, y) that satisfies both equations perfectly.

blocks.title: 2. The Rules: Two Methods
blocks.content:
• **Elimination Method:** Make the coefficients of one variable the same in both equations, then add or subtract to eliminate it.
• **Substitution Method:** Rearrange one equation to express x in terms of y (or vice versa), then substitute into the other.
• Both methods give the same answer. Use whichever feels more natural for the given problem.

blocks.title: 3. Step-by-Step: Elimination Method
blocks.content:
To solve: 2x + 3y = 13 and 4x - 3y = 11:

1. Look at the y-coefficients: +3y and -3y. They're already matched!
2. ADD the equations: (2x + 4x) + (3y - 3y) = 13 + 11.
3. This gives 6x = 24, so x = 4.
4. Substitute x = 4 into equation 1: 2(4) + 3y = 13, so 3y = 5, y = 5/3.
5. Check in equation 2: 4(4) - 3(5/3) = 16 - 5 = 11. Correct!

blocks.title: 4. Worked Example: Substitution Method
blocks.content:
Solve: y = 2x + 1 and 3x + y = 11.

**Step 1:** Equation 1 already gives y in terms of x: y = 2x + 1.
**Step 2:** Substitute into equation 2: 3x + (2x + 1) = 11.
**Step 3:** 5x + 1 = 11, so 5x = 10, x = 2.
**Step 4:** y = 2(2) + 1 = 5.

**Final Answer: x = 2, y = 5.**

blocks.title: 5. Common Pitfalls
blocks.content: The classic elimination mistake: adding when you should subtract (or vice versa). If both equations have +3y, you need to SUBTRACT to eliminate y (3y - 3y = 0). If one has +3y and the other has -3y, you ADD (3y + (-3y) = 0). Also, students often solve for x but forget to find y! Both unknowns must be found for full marks.
